newsitem.title: USA: Harnischfeger says it has other options.
newsitem.headline: Harnischfeger says it has other options.

text.p: Harnischfeger Industries Inc said Friday it remains committed to its "industrial products and services strategy," despite being thwarted in a bid to acquire Giddings & Lewis Inc.
"We have other options, and at this point we're looking at other options," said David Brukardt, a spokesman for Milwaukee-based Harnischfeger.
Giddings, the largest U.S. maker of machine tools, said Thursday it agreed to be acquired by Germany's Thyssen AG for $21 per share, or $675 million plus debt assumption.
Giddings had earlier rejected a $19-per-share bid from Harnischfeger, which had viewed buying Giddings as the launch of a strategic move into industrial products and services.
"Giddings & Lewis was our first pick.... There are no other Giddings," Brukardt said.
"We are very committed to the industrial products and services strategy," he said. "That doesn't necessarily mean we would have to do that with a machine tool maker."
Harnischfeger makes heavy machinery and manufacturing systems for papermaking, mining and materials handling. Revenues in 1996 were $2.9 billion.
